label: Every year around 7 million people die from the stroke.
And you know what? It can happen to anyone at any age.
It happens when the blood flow to the brain is blocked, or a blood vessel in the brain bursts.
Without blood, brain cells start dying within minutes, or about 2 million every minute.
High blood pressure, diabetes, smoking and the stress are the common causes,
but the good news is that it can be prevented.
But first, learn the signs and just remember one word: FAST.
F is Face: does one side droop when they smile?
A is Arms: does one arm drift down or feel weak?
S is Speech: is it slurred or hard to understand?
And also, watch for the sudden dizziness, vision trouble or a severe headache.
And finally, T is the Time.
If you ever see one sign, call 108 or 112 immediately.
Even if they go away, still go to the hospital.
Neither give food, water or medicine, nor wait for it to pass.
This World Stroke Day, 29 October, save this reel and share with your friends and family, as it could save a life.
